title: MetNet: neural rainfall forecasting up to 8 hours ahead
summary: The model forecasts precipitation at 1 km resolution and 2-minute intervals up to 8 hours ahead from radar and satellite, without physical equations. According to the page, it outperforms NOAA’s operational HRRR model up to about 7–8 hours, in seconds rather than about an hour. US coverage only, author-only comparisons, a preprint, and no stated operational use.

evidence.tested: Evaluated on a precipitation-rate forecasting benchmark against NWP (HRRR) and an optical-flow baseline, scored by F1 at 1.0 mm/h; outperforms NWP at forecasts up to about 7 to 8 hours.
evidence.unknown: Demonstrated only for the continental US; the authors call it a small stepping stone; comparisons are author-run.
evidence.ai_role: Deep neural network with axial self-attention forecasting precipitation probabilities from radar and satellite inputs, without physical equations.
